anti_overlap: Do not cover Rust API ergonomics, trait bounds, or derive correctness — those belong to the Rust ergonomics agent
Do not cover SQLite schema design or backend persistence internals — those belong to the persistence agent
Do not cover ACL, scope grants, or cross-Soul identity — those belong to the access-control agent
decision_lens: A game tick is a budget. Every allocation, every syscall, and every block_on is a deduction from that budget. The right integration layer makes the happy path fit the budget with zero tax; the wrong integration layer makes every tick pay for abstractions it doesn't use. The ECS community has learned that 'bolt-on external state stores' fail unless the integration is co-designed with the component model.
focus: ECS integration patterns, per-tick read/write performance budgets, sync-from-async access under pollster::block_on, Soul-as-aggregate vs ECS components mismatch, save-game compatibility, mutation atomicity within a tick
name: fd-ecs-tick-loop-integration
persona: Apply the perspective of a game engine programmer who has integrated third-party data systems into production ECS game loops (hecs, specs, bevy-style), with specific experience in single-threaded tick loops where allocation and blocking are the primary performance enemies.
review_areas: The ported mood_system (§9, naïve port) allocates a Vec<FacetValue> per elf per tick for the new modifier list, plus HashMap clones for each modifier Record. For 8 elves at 100 ticks/sec that is 800 Vec allocs + N*800 HashMap clones per second. The spec acknowledges this and proposes the optimal derivation-based port, but the optimal port requires consumer_tick in DerivationFn (§12, deferred). Until §12 is resolved, the naïve port is the only implementable Phase 1 port — and the spec's claim that 'the mood_system literally vanishes' is premature.

Pattern A (write-through, §8) calls pollster::block_on on every Soul::append in the tick loop. For a MemSoulStore this is a no-op plus one allocation (the Future). For 8 elves × 20 events/tick = 160 block_on calls/tick. At 100 ticks/sec that is 16,000 block_on calls/sec. The spec says 'acceptable for in-memory.' It is — but the caller must know that adding a SqliteSoulStore flips this from acceptble to catastrophic without any API change. The spec should recommend Pattern B (deferred-batch) as the default for any I/O-backed store, not as 'Phase 1.5 opt-in.'

Soul is the 'aggregate' in event-sourcing terms — all mutations go through Soul::append. But in elf-revel's ECS, Personality, Mood, Scars, Relationships are separate components queried independently. The port forces elf-revel to hold a Soul alongside each elf entity, and systems must reach into the Soul's facet map instead of directly borrowing a component. The spec does not address how world.get_soul_mut(soul_id) is implemented — is Soul an ECS component itself? A side-table? The answer materially affects whether ECS parallelism is preserved or broken.

The Heartbreak port (§14) calls soul.append(...) six times per elf per dissolution event. Each append invalidates DerivedCache. If mood.active_modifiers is a registered derivation (the optimal shape), each append re-derives it. For a dissolution event that happens 0-5 times per game, this cost is negligible. But the spec generalizes the pattern: systems that call append multiple times in a tight loop will re-derive on every append. The spec should recommend or enforce 'batch-then-invalidate-once' for multi-append patterns (Soul::replay is already the tool for this).

The spec notes 'elf-revel has no production save path wired' (elf-revel-port-notes.md §Q5) and says 'the Palettice port will be the elf-revel persistence solution.' This means Phase 1 must design the save-game format from scratch. The SqliteSoulStore is the candidate. The spec says elf-revel 'might stay in-memory + snapshot-to-disk' — but this option is not designed anywhere in the spec. If Phase 1 ships only MemSoulStore, elf-revel has no persistence. The Phase 1 acceptance criteria require SqliteSoulStore to pass the shared test suite, but do not require elf-revel to actually use it. This gap should be made explicit.

The §14 port demonstrates that the elf-revel ECS's `world.get_soul_mut(soul_id)` is called in a loop over dissolving pairs. If two dissolution events in the same tick affect the same elf (edge case but possible in a sim), the Soul is mutated twice in the same tick before the durable write happens. With Pattern B (deferred-batch), both batches queue independently and then both block_on at day boundary. The spec does not address whether append_events is idempotent or whether duplicate events from a double-append scenario are a correctness risk.

severity_examples.condition: The spec's §9 optimal port shape (mood_system vanishes, decay is a derivation) requires current_tick in DerivationFn. The locked DerivationFn signature does not carry it. If Phase 1 code starts with the locked signature, every implementation of time-relative derivations must use a workaround (captured Arc<AtomicU64>, closure mutation) that the spec does not anticipate or bless. This is a P0 for the ECS integration because the entire argument that 'the hot path stays sync' depends on derivations being able to compute without store calls — and without tick context, they can't compute ticks_remaining.
severity_examples.scenario: consumer_tick unavailable to derivations, optimal mood port blocked

severity_examples.condition: The spec recommends Pattern A as the Phase 1 default and Pattern B as 'Phase 1.5 opt-in.' If elf-revel ships Phase 1 with SqliteSoulStore and Pattern A, every Soul::append will fsync, making the tick loop I/O-bound at 100 ticks/sec. The spec should invert the default: Pattern B (deferred-batch) is the default for any I/O store; Pattern A is only for MemSoulStore.

The port shapes in §9 and §14 use world.get_soul_mut(soul_id) but this function is not defined anywhere in the spec. Whether Soul is an ECS component, a side-table HashMap<SoulId, Soul>, or a field on a higher-level ElfWorld struct determines whether elf-revel's existing &mut World parallelism is preserved or broken.
severity_examples.scenario: Soul placement in ECS world unspecified

success_hints: Count allocations in the naïve mood-system port per tick per elf, and verify they are in the budget documented in elf-revel-port-notes.md §5
Check that the §8 async/sync interop pattern works correctly when the store is SqliteSoulStore, not just MemSoulStore
Verify that §9 and §14 validation passes can be implemented with the locked DerivationFn signature, or document exactly which locked items must change
Check whether the acceptance criteria in §10 require elf-revel to actually use SqliteSoulStore for persistence, or only that SqliteSoulStore passes a standalone test suite
task_context: elf-revel is the Phase 1 integration target — a running ~9700-LOC Rust ECS sim with a single-threaded tick loop at 100 ticks/sec, 8-50 elves, ~40 systems. The reviewer should check that the locked API (§1-4) is actually usable inside this tick loop without performance regressions, and that the §8 interop pattern is sufficient for Phase 1.
